desire_motivation_analysis.reasoning_chain: When person_long_hair describes the abuse, person_cap immediately interrupts. He does not deny the event occurred but focuses entirely on how the description makes him 'look.' This indicates a desire to avoid shame/reputation damage rather than a desire to resolve the conflict.

supporting_evidence.description: Interrupts immediately after the description of violence.
Says 'Why are you trying to make me look so bad?' explicitly focusing on image.

alternative_interpretations.reasoning: He might just want to stop the argument.
alternative_interpretations.why_not_primary: His language is specific to his image ('make me look bad'), not the conflict itself.

desire_motivation_analysis.reasoning_chain: Once the facts are established, person_cap shifts from denying the appearance of abuse to justifying the abuse itself. He asserts ownership over the interaction ('She doesn't get to leave'), indicating a desire for control and dominance over the partner's autonomy.

supporting_evidence.description: Claims 'She makes me react that way.'
Explicitly states 'She doesn't get to leave when I'm still angry.'

desire_motivation_analysis.reasoning_chain: Person_long_hair recounts the story to the therapist (a third party authority). The detailed description of the purse throwing and blocking is an attempt to have her reality acknowledged and validated by an outside observer.

supporting_evidence.description: Maintains gaze on therapist while speaking, ignoring person_cap.

desire_motivation_analysis.reasoning_chain: The therapist interrupts the emotional deflection to ask a binary question ('Did you do that?'). This indicates a motivation to strip away the emotional manipulation and establish the objective reality of the event.

supporting_evidence.description: Holds up hand to stop person_cap speaking.
Directs conversation to 'stick to the facts.'

trigger_event.description: Therapist forces a binary 'yes/no' answer regarding the physical abuse.

behavioral_markers.description: Expression shifts from incredulous/defensive to aggressive/accusatory.
Uses hand to point at partner while blaming her.

desire_transitions.visual_marker_of_change: The moment person_cap realizes he cannot deny the fact, he leans forward and points his finger to shift blame.
desire_transitions.psychological_interpretation: When the strategy of denial/obfuscation (Reputation Defense) fails due to the therapist's fact-checking, the subject shifts to a secondary defense mechanism: rationalizing the behavior as a necessary response to the victim's actions (Dominance Justification/DARVO).

behavioral_sequence.behavior_description: Furrowed brows, mouth open in disbelief, shaking head
behavioral_sequence.relevance_to_desire: Supports Esteem_Reputation_Defense by acting as the aggrieved party.
Supports Social_Dominance_Assertion; emphasizes his emotional state prioritizes her physical freedom.

key_segments_for_qa.segment_description: Therapist confronts the husband with facts; husband attempts to deflect.
key_segments_for_qa.psychological_significance: Demonstrates the conflict between Epistemic_Truth_Verification (Therapist) and Epistemic_Obfuscation (Husband).

key_segments_for_qa.segment_description: Husband admits to preventing wife from leaving because he was angry.
key_segments_for_qa.psychological_significance: Clear display of coercive control motivation overriding social norms.

inter_character_dynamics.mutual_influence: Person_cap exerts coercive control; Person_long_hair exhibits learned helplessness/defensiveness.

key_interaction_moments.description: Person_long_hair describes person_cap throwing her purse.

annotation_metadata.annotation_notes: The video is a skit performed by a single actress playing three roles. Annotation treats them as distinct psychological entities based on costume and role. The 'Husband' character displays classic narcissistic behavioral patterns (DARVO, gaslighting), making desire inference relatively straightforward based on clinical models of abuse.
